rules.name: Questionnaire flow overview
rules.statement: The questionnaire is in English and asks each piece of information once. Steps in order: (1) Personal details - first name, last name, date of birth. (2) Home address - street, house number, postcode, town, country; canton only if living in Switzerland. (3) Start - first working day. (4) Civil status - civil status; spouse's/partner's date of birth if married, in a registered partnership or separated. (5) Source tax status - only for employees living in Switzerland: nationality; C permit if not Swiss; for non-Swiss without C permit who are married or in a registered partnership: spouse's nationality, spouse's C permit if not Swiss, spouse's country of residence if Swiss or C permit. (6) Source tax details - only if subject to source tax: confession; spouse works (married/registered partnership); children and the per-child questions (repeated per child); then cross-border questions for residents of Germany or Liechtenstein. (7) End - permit reminder for non-Swiss employees and everyone living abroad. On submission answers that no longer apply are discarded and the questionnaire becomes read-only for the employee; derived results are computed from the latest answers.

table.then: Everyone: first name, last name, date of birth.
Everyone: street, house number, postcode, town, country. Canton only if the country is Switzerland.
Everyone: first working day (insurance start date is derived, not asked).
Everyone: civil status. Spouse's/partner's date of birth if Married, Registered partnership or Separated.

Only employees living in Switzerland: nationality; C permit (non-Swiss); spouse nationality, spouse C permit, spouse country of residence (non-Swiss without C permit, married or registered partnership). Employees abroad skip this step.

Only if subject to source tax: confession; spouse works (married/registered partnership); has children and per-child questions; residence-dependent questions for Germany (daily return, certificate of residence, reasonable return, more than 60 non-return days) or Liechtenstein (daily return, more than 45 non-return days).
Permit reminder for non-Swiss employees and all employees living abroad; submission.

rules.name: Insurance start date
rules.statement: The pension fund insurance start date is derived from the first working day: if the first working day is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day; otherwise on the 1st of the following month (e.g. 15.03 gives 01.04). It is always derived again from the latest first working day, so a moved start date updates it.

table.then: Insurance start date = first working day

when: is not the 1st of a month
table.then: Insurance start date = 1st of the following month

rules.name: Civil status entered at the pension fund
rules.statement: The fund only offers Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed. Provisionally, Registered partnership and Separated are entered as Married (with the partner's/spouse's date of birth); the other values are entered as given.

rules.name: Subject to source tax
rules.statement: An employee living abroad is subject to source tax regardless of nationality. An employee living in Switzerland is subject only if not a Swiss citizen (anyone with Swiss citizenship counts as Swiss), without a C permit, and not married to / in a registered partnership with a Swiss citizen or C-permit holder who lives in Switzerland. Only employees subject to source tax are asked the source tax questions. Liechtenstein residents count as subject (they are asked the questions); their result may still be 'in principle no source tax liability'.
rules.expression: (is_set(address_country) and address_country != "Switzerland") or (address_country == "Switzerland" and holds_c_permit == "no" and not (civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and (spouse_nationality == "Switzerland" or spouse_holds_c_permit == "yes") and spouse_residence_country == "Switzerland"))

rules.name: Civil status group for source tax
rules.statement: For source tax, Married and Registered partnership count as 'married or registered partnership'; Single, Divorced, Widowed and Separated count as 'single, divorced, separated or widowed'.
rules.expression: if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], "Married or registered partnership", if_else(civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"], "Single, divorced, separated or widowed", null))

rules.name: Residence for source tax
rules.statement: The calculator's residence answer is derived from the country of the home address: Switzerland, Germany, Liechtenstein, or any other country. Switzerland and other countries lead straight to the base tariff; Germany and Liechtenstein have their own follow-up questions.
rules.expression: if_else(address_country == "Switzerland", "Switzerland", if_else(address_country == "Germany", "Germany", if_else(address_country == "Liechtenstein", "Liechtenstein", if_else(is_set(address_country), "Other country", null))))

rules.name: Church-tax suffix
rules.statement: The tariff code ends in Y for Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed, and N for none or other.

when: Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed

rules.expression: if_else(confession == "Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed", "Y", if_else(confession == "None or other", "N", null))

rules.name: Per-child result
rules.statement: Each child is evaluated on its own: it counts, counts with H (single group only), or does not count. Rows marked as inferred were not observed in the calculator and must be checked before go-live (OQ-calculator-coverage).
rules.expression: if_else(calculator_civil_status == "Single, divorced, separated or widowed" and ((child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_custody == "Sole custody") or (child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_common_household_other_parent == "no" and child_alternating_custody == "no") or child_main_financial_contributor == "Employee" or (child_age_status == "Adult in first education" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_maintenance_over_50 == "yes")), "counts with H", if_else((calculator_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership" and ((child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_custody == "Sole custody") or child_common_household_other_parent == "yes" or child_main_financial_contributor == "Employee" or child_maintenance_over_50 == "yes")) or (calculator_civil_status == "Single, divorced, separated or widowed" and child_age_status == "Adult in first education" and child_same_household == "no" and child_maintenance_over_50 == "yes"), "counts", "does not count"))

rules.name: Child digit of the tariff code
rules.statement: The digit of the tariff code is the number of children whose per-child result is 'counts' or 'counts with H'; 0 if the employee has no children. (The expression shows the contribution of one child; for several children the contributions are added up.)

table.then: Number of children that count (with or without H)

rules.expression: if_else(has_children == "yes" and child_result in ["counts", "counts with H"], 1, 0)

rules.name: Base tariff letter
rules.statement: Married or registered partnership: C if the spouse/partner works or receives replacement income, otherwise B. Single, divorced, separated or widowed: H if any child counts with H, otherwise A. Tariffs G and Q (replacement income) and special tariffs such as D do not occur in onboarding.
rules.expression: if_else(calculator_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership", if_else(spouse_gainful_employment == "yes", "C", "B"), if_else(child_result == "counts with H", "H", "A"))

rules.name: Cross-border (Grenzgänger) tariff applies
rules.statement: For employees living in Germany the cross-border tariff applies if they return daily and have handed in a certificate of residence ('not yet' counts as no), or if they do not return daily, a daily return would be reasonable, and they do not expect more than 60 non-return days. In all other cases (and for all other countries) the normal tariff applies.
rules.expression: calculator_residence == "Germany" and ((daily_return_germany == "yes" and residence_certificate == "yes") or (daily_return_germany == "no" and daily_return_reasonable == "yes" and non_return_days_60 == "no"))

rules.name: Final tariff letter
rules.statement: If the cross-border tariff applies, the base letter is replaced: A by L, B by M, C by N, H by P. Otherwise the base letter is used.

rules.name: Liechtenstein: in principle no source tax liability
rules.statement: An employee living in Liechtenstein who returns daily, or does not return daily but expects at most 45 work-related non-return days, gets 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' instead of a tariff code, flagged for HR. With more than 45 non-return days the normal tariff code applies.

table.then: In principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement (flag for HR)
In principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement (flag for HR)

rules.name: Source tax tariff code
rules.statement: For every employee subject to source tax Lonio computes the Zurich tariff code from the answers: final tariff letter + child digit + church-tax suffix (e.g. A0N, C1Y, L0Y, N1Y). For Liechtenstein residents with daily return or at most 45 non-return days the result is 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' instead, flagged for HR. Employees not subject to source tax get no tariff code. The result is always derived again from the latest answers and is recorded for HR.

table.then: 'In principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR
Tariff letter + child digit + church-tax suffix

rules.expression: if_else(subject_to_source_tax, if_else(liechtenstein_no_source_tax, "in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement", [tariff_letter, child_count, church_tax_suffix]), null)

rules.name: Permit reminder
rules.statement: At the end of the questionnaire every non-Swiss employee and every employee living abroad (whatever their nationality, as it is not asked of them) is reminded to bring their permit on the first working day. HR words the reminder so that a Swiss citizen living abroad can see it does not apply to them. It collects no data.

rules.name: Discard answers that no longer apply
rules.statement: If the employee changes an earlier answer so that a later question no longer applies, its answer may be kept while the employee goes back and forth, but is discarded on submission. No personal data that no party needs is kept.

rules.name: Read-only after submission
rules.statement: After submission the questionnaire is read-only for the employee. Later changes (move, marriage, new child, certificate of residence handed in later, corrected nationality, moved first working day) are made by HR (later HR-side spec). Every derived result - insurance start date, civil status for the fund and for source tax, subject to source tax, tariff code - is always derived again from the latest answers; for the first working day only the latest date counts and no history is kept.

feature.title: Employee onboarding questionnaire
feature.goal: A new employee at Muster AG answers one short English questionnaire in Lonio that asks each piece of information once, and only when a receiving party needs it for that person. From those answers Lonio records everything HR, Pensionskasse Muster and the Zurich source tax office need, including the derived insurance start date and the computed source tax tariff code.
feature.context:
Today Muster AG's HR collects onboarding data for several receiving parties: the pension fund registration (Pensionskasse Muster portal), the source tax tariff (the Canton of Zurich calculator, which HR clicks through by hand) and HR's own needs, such as a complete postal address for posting documents. Pain points stated by the sources:
- The first working day is HR's 'number one' item, and it often moves (for example when an earlier exit is negotiated with the old employer). The pension fund insurance start date depends on it (F-hr_transcript-872bd7, F-hr_transcript-1d5c07, F-hr_transcript-e18e66).
- Incomplete addresses block posted documents (F-hr_transcript-c0fe95).
- The pension fund's required fields (Canton, Civil status, Spouse's date of birth) do not fit every case: employees abroad, registered partnerships, separated employees (F-pension_portal-b359c3, F-pension_portal-3d1ae4).
- HR's rule for who is subject to source tax took several corrections to state (F-hr_transcript-5af8d0, F-hr_transcript-550840).
- Determining the tariff code is a manual, multi-branch calculator walk-through: civil status, spouse employment, children, confession and the cross-border cases for Germany and Liechtenstein.

Lonio replaces this. It asks each item once and only when a party needs it (data minimisation, G-01). It derives values instead of asking for them (G-08). It computes the full tariff code itself (D-001).

Scope: the employee side of the questionnaire only (G-04, D-034).

Out of scope:
- transmission of the data to the parties
- HR screens and HR changes after submission
- AHV data and IT equipment (G-03)
- the photo for employee badges
- document uploads (D-035)
- income type and replacement income (D-006)
- special tariffs (D-009)

Decisions to follow:
- D-005: only 'C permit yes/no' is asked, never the permit type.
- D-003: registered partnership and separated are mapped provisionally for the fund.
- D-007: Liechtenstein residents may get 'in principle no source tax liability'.
- D-036, D-037: on submission, answers that no longer apply are discarded and the questionnaire becomes read-only. Derived results are always computed from the latest answers.

sections.title: Questionnaire flow overview
sections.purpose: Give the employee one English questionnaire with fixed steps, where each question appears only under its condition. At the end come the permit reminder and a submission that discards answers that no longer apply and makes the questionnaire read-only.

stories.title: Show the source tax step only to employees who are subject to source tax
stories.i_want: the source tax details step (confession, spouse works, children, cross-border questions) to appear only for employees who are subject to source tax
stories.so_that: I no longer have to work out up front who must answer the source tax questions, and employees who are not subject are not asked for personal data no party needs
stories.priority_reason: HR's stated pain: 'I never know up front who has to answer those questions' (F-hr_transcript-b84498). Asking everyone would also break data minimisation (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees subject to source tax get the source tax details step
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee who, from the answers in the earlier steps, is subject to source tax: living abroad (whatever the nationality), or living in Switzerland without Swiss citizenship, without a C permit and not married to / in a registered partnership with a Swiss citizen or C-permit holder who lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax details step
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked the confession and whether they have children (with the per-child questions for each child); married employees and registered partners are also asked whether their spouse or partner works. No income type is asked: a new employee always has earned income (D-006). The tariff code is computed by Lonio from these answers, not asked (D-001).

examples.name: Non-Swiss single employee without C permit living in Switzerland
Non-Swiss married employee whose C-permit spouse lives abroad
Separated non-Swiss employee without C permit (counts as single for source tax)

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees not subject to source tax skip the source tax details step
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Switzerland who holds Swiss citizenship (also with another nationality), or holds a C permit, or is married to / in a registered partnership with a Swiss citizen or C-permit holder who lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee completes the source tax status step
acceptance_criteria.then: the source tax details step is skipped entirely: no confession, children, spouse-works or cross-border questions are asked.

examples.name: Registered partner of a C-permit holder living in Switzerland

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border questions only for residents of Germany or Liechtenstein
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee who is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: the source tax details step reaches the cross-border questions (after the children questions)
acceptance_criteria.then: employees living in Germany are asked the German cross-border questions (daily return, then certificate of residence, reasonable return or more than 60 non-return days as they apply); employees living in Liechtenstein are asked the Liechtenstein questions (daily return, then more than 45 non-return days); employees living in Switzerland or any other country get no cross-border questions. Liechtenstein residents are asked these questions even though their result may be 'in principle no source tax liability' (D-007).

examples.name: Non-Swiss employee without C permit living in Switzerland

stories.title: Ask the steps in an order that avoids unneeded questions
stories.i_want: to go through fixed steps in a set order, where every question only appears once the earlier answers show that a receiving party needs it for me
stories.so_that: I answer a short questionnaire without questions that do not apply to me
stories.priority_reason: The flow overview is a required part of the feature; asking too little blocks a registration and asking too much collects data we must not have (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Fixed order of the steps
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee opens the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through it
acceptance_criteria.then: the steps come in this order: (1) Personal details - first name, last name, date of birth; (2) Home address - street, house number, postcode, town, country, and the canton if living in Switzerland; (3) Start - first working day; (4) Civil status - civil status and, where it applies, the spouse's or partner's date of birth; (5) Source tax status - only for employees living in Switzerland; (6) Source tax details - only for employees subject to source tax; (7) End - permit reminder where it applies, then submission. The questionnaire is in English.

acceptance_criteria.title: Canton only for employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is in the home address step
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee gives the country of the home address
acceptance_criteria.then: the canton is asked only if the country is Switzerland; employees living abroad are not asked for a canton (provisional, see OQ-canton-abroad).

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's or partner's date of birth only for married, registered partners and separated employees
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is in the civil status step
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee gives the civil status (Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed, Registered partnership or Separated)
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's or partner's date of birth is asked only for Married, Registered partnership and Separated; it is not asked for Single, Divorced or Widowed (see OQ-spouse-dob-other-status and OQ-civil-status-partnership).

acceptance_criteria.title: Source tax status step only for employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has completed the civil status step
acceptance_criteria.when: the source tax status step would start
acceptance_criteria.then: employees living abroad skip it entirely (they are subject to source tax whatever their nationality, so nationality is not asked). Employees living in Switzerland are asked their nationality ('Switzerland' for anyone holding Swiss citizenship); only non-Swiss employees are then asked whether they hold a C permit (yes or no). The permit type itself is never asked (D-005).

examples.name: Swiss citizen living in Germany (like Stefan, hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a)

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse questions only when they can change the source tax outcome
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Switzerland who is not Swiss
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee has answered the C permit question
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's or partner's nationality is asked only if the employee has no C permit and is Married or in a Registered partnership; the spouse's C permit (yes or no) only if the spouse is not Swiss; the spouse's country of residence only if the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit. Separated employees are not asked these questions, as they count as single for source tax (D-003).

examples.name: Married, spouse not Swiss and without C permit

acceptance_criteria.title: Questions that no party needs are never asked
acceptance_criteria.given: any employee
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is never asked for the income type or replacement income (D-006), the permit type (D-005), social insurance (AHV) data, IT equipment, a badge photo or document uploads. The insurance start date, the subject-to-source-tax result and the tariff code are derived, not asked (G-08).

stories.title: Ask each piece of information once and reuse it for every receiving party
stories.i_want: to give each piece of information only once, even when several receiving parties need it
stories.so_that: I do not repeat myself, and HR, Pensionskasse Muster and source tax all get consistent answers from the same source
stories.priority_reason: Core goal of the feature (G-01); today HR collects spouse details by email in a slow separate round (F-hr_transcript-a45422).

acceptance_criteria.title: Each question appears once
acceptance_criteria.given: any employee
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through all steps
acceptance_criteria.then: each piece of information is asked in exactly one step and never asked again later in the questionnaire, and every question is in English.

acceptance_criteria.title: One answer feeds every party that needs it
acceptance_criteria.given: an answer needed by more than one receiving party
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee gives it
acceptance_criteria.then: the same answer is recorded for every party that needs it: the country of the home address serves HR's postal address, the pension fund's canton condition and source tax; the civil status serves the pension fund's civil status and the source tax civil status group (registered partnership counts as married and separated as single for source tax, D-003); the first working day serves HR and the derived insurance start date.

Registered partner without C permit: one civil status answer, two uses
Employee living in Germany: country answer used for canton and source tax

stories.title: Remind non-Swiss employees and employees living abroad to bring their permit
stories.i_want: the questionnaire to end with a reminder to bring the permit on the first working day for every non-Swiss employee and every employee living abroad
stories.so_that: fewer new employees forget their permit on their first day
stories.priority_reason: Explicit HR wish ('half of them forget', F-hr_transcript-c53552); it saves HR follow-up but blocks no registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Who sees the permit reminder
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee reaches the end of the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the reminder is decided
acceptance_criteria.then: employees living in Switzerland who are not Swiss citizens see the reminder; every employee living abroad sees it, whatever their nationality (nationality is not asked of them); Swiss citizens living in Switzerland do not see it.

examples.name: Swiss citizen living in Germany (like Stefan, hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a)

acceptance_criteria.title: The reminder collects no data and is worded by HR
acceptance_criteria.given: the reminder is shown
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reads it
acceptance_criteria.then: it only reminds the employee to bring their permit on the first working day; it asks nothing and records no answer. HR provides the wording, so that a Swiss citizen living abroad can see that it does not apply to them. No extra 'Swiss citizen' question is added just for the reminder.

stories.title: Discard answers that no longer apply on submission
stories.i_want: to change earlier answers without losing my input while I go back and forth, and to have answers to questions that no longer apply dropped when I submit
stories.so_that: I can correct myself easily, and no personal data that no receiving party needs is kept about me
stories.priority_reason: Data minimisation is a hard constraint: collecting data we must not have is a stated risk (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers are kept while the employee goes back and forth
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered a question and then changes an earlier answer so that the question no longer applies
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee changes the earlier answer back before submitting
acceptance_criteria.then: the question applies again and the previously given answer is still there; no input is lost.

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers to questions that no longer apply are discarded on submission
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answers to questions that no longer apply after a change of an earlier answer
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee submits the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: only answers to questions that apply to the submitted answers are recorded; all other answers are discarded and not recorded for any party.

examples.name: Employee first entered Switzerland and an Italian nationality, then changed the country to Germany
Employee first chose Married and gave a spouse's date of birth, then changed to Single
Non-Swiss employee first answered no C permit and the source tax details, then changed to yes

stories.title: Make the questionnaire read-only after submission and derive results from the latest answers
stories.i_want: the questionnaire to become read-only for the employee once submitted, and every derived result to be derived again from the latest answers
stories.so_that: later changes go through HR, and derived values such as the insurance start date never go stale at the receiving parties
stories.priority_reason: A missed update after Julia's first working day moved caused a wrong date at the pension fund, an unfriendly letter and weeks of fixing (F-hr_transcript-e18e66).

acceptance_criteria.title: The employee cannot change answers after submission
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee opens it again
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee can see the answers but cannot change them. Later changes (a move, a marriage, a new child, a certificate of residence handed in later, a corrected nationality, a moved first working day) are made by HR; how HR does this is part of the later HR-side spec (D-034).

acceptance_criteria.title: Derived results always follow the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: an answer recorded for an employee is changed after submission
acceptance_criteria.when: the derived results are looked at
acceptance_criteria.then: the insurance start date, the civil status for the pension fund and for source tax, whether the employee is subject to source tax, and the tariff code are all derived again from the latest answers. For the first working day only the latest date counts; no history of earlier dates is kept.

sections.title: Personal details and home address
sections.purpose: Collect the employee's name, date of birth and complete home address once. HR uses them to post documents and the pension fund to register the employee. The country of the address decides which later questions apply, and the canton is asked only of employees living in Switzerland.

stories.title: Collect the employee's name and date of birth
stories.i_want: every new employee to give their first name, last name and date of birth in the onboarding questionnaire
stories.so_that: the employee can be registered for the occupational pension: the registration cannot be submitted without these required fields. HR also uses the name to identify the employee and to address posted documents
stories.priority_reason: First name, last name and date of birth are required fields of the pension fund registration. The registration is rejected without them ('<Field> is required.'), so missing values block it.

acceptance_criteria.title: First and last name are asked of every employee and cannot be left empty
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire, whatever their country of residence, nationality or civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the personal details
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire asks for the first name and the last name. Both are required, and the questionnaire cannot be submitted while either is empty. The names are recorded for the pension fund registration (its required 'First name' and 'Last name' fields) and for HR, which uses them to identify the employee and address posted documents

acceptance_criteria.title: Date of birth is asked of every employee as a date DD.MM.YYYY
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the personal details
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire asks for the employee's date of birth as a date in the form DD.MM.YYYY (e.g. 14.03.1990). It is required, and the questionnaire cannot be submitted without it. The date of birth is recorded for the pension fund registration (its required 'Date of birth' field)

acceptance_criteria.title: Name and date of birth are asked once only
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered their name and date of birth
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues through the rest of the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: no later step asks for the employee's own name or date of birth again. The same answers serve both the pension fund and HR

stories.title: Collect a complete postal home address
stories.i_want: every new employee to give their full home address: street, house number, postcode, town and country
stories.so_that: HR can post documents to the employee without chasing missing address parts
stories.priority_reason: HR posts a lot of documents to employees and states that the address 'has to be complete'. An incomplete address blocks posting.

acceptance_criteria.title: All five parts of the home address are asked of every employee and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire, whether they live in Switzerland or abroad
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the home address
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire asks for the street, house number, postcode, town and country of the home address. All five are required, and the questionnaire cannot be submitted while any part is missing. The address is recorded for HR to post documents

acceptance_criteria.title: The address is a normal postal address, nothing more
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee enters their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire asks for the address
acceptance_criteria.then: it asks only for what is written on an envelope (street, house number, postcode, town, country) and no further address details. Whether every address has a house number is not stated by any source, so the house number stays required as HR listed it

acceptance_criteria.title: The country is named in English
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee enters the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee chooses or states the country
acceptance_criteria.then: the country is recorded by its English name, e.g. "Switzerland", "Germany", "Liechtenstein"

stories.title: Use the home address country as the country of residence
stories.i_want: the country of the employee's home address to serve as their country of residence, without a separate question
stories.so_that: Lonio can tell whether the employee lives in Switzerland or abroad. That decides who is subject to source tax, which follow-up questions apply (nationality, canton, the cross-border questions for Germany and Liechtenstein), and the tariff code Lonio computes
stories.priority_reason: Employees living abroad are always subject to source tax. Without the country of residence neither source tax liability nor the tariff code can be determined, and HR says it never knows up front who has to answer the source tax questions.

acceptance_criteria.title: The country of residence is not asked separately
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire needs the employee's country of residence (for source tax or for the pension fund's canton)
acceptance_criteria.then: it uses the country of the home address and does not ask a separate country-of-residence question

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living abroad are subject to source tax whatever their nationality
acceptance_criteria.given: the country of the home address is not Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether the employee is subject to source tax (rule subject_to_source_tax, owned by the source tax section)
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is subject to source tax, and their nationality is not asked. This includes Swiss citizens living abroad (e.g. Stefan) and Liechtenstein residents. acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living in Switzerland get the residence-dependent questions
acceptance_criteria.given: the country of the home address is Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked for the canton (see US-02.4) and for their nationality, which decides source tax liability for residents (owned by another section). The cross-border questions for Germany and Liechtenstein are not asked

acceptance_criteria.title: Germany and Liechtenstein lead to their cross-border questions
acceptance_criteria.given: the country of the home address is Germany or Liechtenstein
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked that country's cross-border questions, starting with whether they return home daily (owned by the source tax section). Employees living in any other country abroad are asked neither set. This follows the calculator's residence options Germany, Liechtenstein and other country

stories.so_that: the required 'Canton' field of the pension fund registration can be filled, while employees abroad are not asked for a canton they do not have

acceptance_criteria.title: The canton is asked and required only of employees living in Switzerland

acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire decides whether to ask for the canton
acceptance_criteria.then: if the country is Switzerland, the canton is asked and required. Otherwise it is not asked. What the fund expects for employees living abroad, and whether 'Canton' means canton of residence or of work, is still open (see OQ-canton-abroad, non-blocking)

acceptance_criteria.title: The canton is one of the fund's 26 Swiss cantons

sections.title: Source tax: residence abroad and cross-border questions
sections.purpose: Derive the calculator's residence answer from the home address. Germany residents are asked the cross-border questions (daily return, certificate of residence, reasonable return, more than 60 non-return days), which decide the cross-border tariff. Liechtenstein residents are asked about daily return and more than 45 non-return days, which can lead to 'in principle no source tax liability' flagged for HR.

stories.title: Derive the calculator's residence answers from the home address
stories.i_want: Lonio to derive the source tax calculator's residence answers (main residence in Switzerland, and otherwise Germany, Liechtenstein or another country) from the country of the employee's home address, without asking the employee a separate residence question
stories.so_that: the employee is asked where they live only once. Lonio can then pick the right cross-border follow-up questions and compute the tariff code, and I no longer have to work through the calculator's residence block by hand
stories.priority_reason: Every other residence-dependent question and the computed tariff code (D-001) depend on this. HR finds the questions for employees living abroad hard to keep track of today (F-hr_transcript-8595fb).

acceptance_criteria.title: Residence for source tax is derived from the country of the home address
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has entered the country of their home address (the address is asked of everyone and owned by the address section)
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio determines the residence answer that the source tax calculator would ask for
acceptance_criteria.then: The residence is 'Switzerland' if the country is Switzerland, 'Germany' if it is Germany, 'Liechtenstein' if it is Liechtenstein, and 'Other country' for any other country. The employee is not asked a separate residence or country-of-residence question for source tax.

acceptance_criteria.title: Switzerland and other countries get no cross-border questions
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee lives in Switzerland or in a country other than Germany or Liechtenstein
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through the source tax part of the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: None of the Germany questions (daily return, certificate of residence, reasonable return, more than 60 non-return days) and none of the Liechtenstein questions (daily return, more than 45 non-return days) are asked. The tariff code is computed from the base tariff, as in the calculator.

acceptance_criteria.title: Changing the country of residence removes the cross-border answers on submission
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee answered the Germany or Liechtenstein questions and then changes the country of their home address to another country
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee submits the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: Answers to cross-border questions that no longer apply are not kept. Until submission they may be kept, so that going back and forth loses no input.

stories.title: Germany: daily return and certificate of residence
stories.i_want: employees living in Germany to be asked whether they return daily to their main residence in Germany and, if they do, whether they have handed in a certificate of residence
stories.so_that: the cross-border (Grenzgänger) tariff is applied only when the calculator's conditions are met, and the normal tariff is applied otherwise
stories.priority_reason: Without these answers Lonio cannot compute the tariff code for employees living in Germany (D-001). HR cannot remember these questions today (F-hr_transcript-8595fb).

acceptance_criteria.title: Daily return to Germany is asked only of employees living in Germany
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is subject to source tax (everyone living abroad is)
acceptance_criteria.when: the country of their home address is Germany
acceptance_criteria.then: The employee is asked whether they return daily to their main residence in Germany, answered 'yes' or 'no'. The answer is required. Employees living in any other country are not asked. The answer is recorded for source tax (the cross-border tariff decision).

acceptance_criteria.title: Certificate of residence is asked only after a daily return
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Germany is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: they answer that they return daily to their main residence in Germany
acceptance_criteria.then: They are asked whether they have handed in a certificate of residence, answered 'yes', 'no' or 'not yet'. The answer is required. Employees who do not return daily are not asked. The certificate itself goes to HR outside Lonio; nothing is uploaded.

acceptance_criteria.title: Daily return with a certificate gives the cross-border tariff; without one, the normal tariff
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Germany who is subject to source tax returns daily to their main residence in Germany
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio computes the tariff code
acceptance_criteria.then: If the certificate of residence has been handed in ('yes'), the cross-border tariff applies. If the answer is 'no' or 'not yet', the normal tariff applies. Employees living outside Germany always get the normal tariff from this rule. The cross-border result changes the tariff letter (A to L, B to M, C to N, H to P; see the tariff letter rule). The A/B/H paths are verified before go-live (see OQ-calculator-coverage).

flow.intro: The questionnaire has 7 steps, in English. Only applicable questions are shown, and a step with no applicable question is skipped (e.g. steps 5 and 6 for employees not subject to source tax). Each piece of information is asked once and reused for every receiving party. The order follows dependencies: the home country and civil status come first, because they decide who is asked about nationality, C permit, spouse, source tax details and cross-border questions. Answers that no longer apply after a change are discarded on submission (D-036).

steps.title: Personal details
steps.asks: First name, last name and date of birth.

steps.title: Home address
steps.asks: Street, house number, postcode, town and country of residence; the canton only if the country is Switzerland.

steps.title: Civil status
steps.asks: Civil status (Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed, Registered partnership, Separated); the spouse's or partner's date of birth only if married, in a registered partnership or separated.

steps.title: Source tax status
steps.asks: Nationality; whether the employee holds a C permit, only if not Swiss. If not Swiss, without a C permit, and married or in a registered partnership: the spouse's or partner's nationality, whether they hold a C permit (only if not Swiss), and their country of residence (only if Swiss or C permit holder).

steps.title: Source tax details
steps.asks: Religious denomination; whether the spouse or partner works or receives replacement income (only if married or in a registered partnership); whether the employee has children, then for each child the age status, household, custody, care, maintenance and contribution questions that apply to that child; then cross-border questions: for residents of Germany, daily return, certificate of residence (if returning daily; 'not yet' is valid), whether daily return is reasonable and more than 60 non-return days expected (if not returning daily); for residents of Liechtenstein, daily return and more than 45 non-return days expected (if not returning daily).
steps.shown_to: Employees subject to source tax (residents of Liechtenstein are included)

steps.title: End
steps.asks: Nothing is asked; the employee is reminded to bring their permit on the first working day.
steps.shown_to: Non-Swiss employees and everyone living abroad (the reminder is worded so that a Swiss citizen living abroad sees it does not apply)

flow.closing: On submission, answers that no longer apply are discarded and the questionnaire becomes read-only for the employee. The answers are recorded for HR. The insurance start date, civil status for the fund and for source tax, subject to source tax and the tariff code (or the Liechtenstein 'in principle no source tax liability' result, flagged for HR) are derived from the latest answers. Later changes are made by HR.
